# 重治毗尼事義集要

**ID:** X0719
**Volume:** X40
**Category:** 律部類
**Original Category:** 大小乘釋律部／小乘律疏
**Byline:** 明 智旭輯繹
**Dynasty:** 明
**Date:** 1368–1644
**Juans:** 17
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/X0719

## Contributors
- 智旭 (A001257)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A seventeen-fascicle revised digest of *Sìfēnlǜ* 四分律 vinaya material compiled by **Ǒuyì Zhìxù** 蕅益智旭 ([智旭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%97%AD), 1599–1655), the late-Míng integrative Buddhist master who is one of the *Wǎn-Míng sì dà gāosēng* 晚明四大高僧 ("Four Great Masters of Late Míng Buddhism"). The work is a *chóngzhì* 重治 ("re-edited") version of an earlier compilation by Zhìxù; the post-colophon note in the source records that the original ran to eighteen *juan*, with the eighteenth (*Jièdù lüèshì* 犍度略釋) circulating separately and edited in this Manji recension as a stand-alone work ([KR6k0174](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0174)).

**Abstract**

The *Jíyào* digests, classifies, and re-arranges the standard *Sìfēn* vinaya material — pātimokkha, *jiémó* 羯磨 (karmavācanā), *jiēdù* 犍度 (skandhaka) — in a form designed for late-Míng monastic use. Zhìxù was active in Vinaya scholarship throughout his career: the work belongs together with his *Píní shìyì yàolüè* 毗尼事義要略 and *Sìfēnlǜzàng dàxiǎo chíjiè jiēdù lüèshì* ([KR6k0174](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0174)) as a coherent late-Míng programme of Vinaya synthesis. As a Tiāntái-Chán-Pure Land synthesist, Zhìxù was atypical among Vinaya commentators of his generation: his interest in the Vinaya was framed by the late-Míng concern (shared with Zhūhóng, Hānshān Déqīng, and the Bǎohuáshān revivalists) for restoring observant monastic discipline as the precondition for meditative and devotional practice. The text was eventually integrated into the *Bǎohuáshān* Vinaya curriculum and supplied with a follow-up gloss, *Píní guānyào* 毗尼關要 ([KR6k0152](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6k/KR6k0152)), by **Dìngān Déjī** 定菴德基 ([德基](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BE%B7%E5%9F%BA), 1634–1700/01).
